criteria_coverage.criterion: AC1: Authenticated request returns 200 with PDF bytes, Content-Type application/pdf, and Content-Disposition attachment with filename reflecting resource name
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 200 with PDF content-type and content-disposition when resource and file exist
criteria_coverage.notes: Test asserts 200, Content-Type contains application/pdf, Content-Disposition contains 'attachment' and the resource name ('Lesson Plan'), and body byteLength > 0. Gap (non-blocking): does not explicitly assert the filename carries a .pdf extension (contract says filename="<name>.pdf"), and does not assert filename is enclosed in quotes. A subtly buggy implementation that emitted 'attachment; Lesson Plan' or omitted .pdf would still pass.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC2: Unauthenticated download returns 401 with JSON error body and delivers no bytes
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 401 with JSON error body for unauthenticated request
src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not increment download count on 401
criteria_coverage.notes: 401 status, JSON content-type, and body.error asserted. 'No file bytes' is only implied by the 401 body being JSON — not explicitly asserted that no application/pdf bytes are sent. Minor.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC3: Non-existent resource returns 404 with JSON error body
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 404 with JSON error body for non-existent resource
src/app/api/resources/[id]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 404 with JSON error body for unknown resource
criteria_coverage.notes: Both the download and metadata routes cover 404 + JSON.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC4: Resource exists but file missing → 5xx JSON error body, counter NOT incremented
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 5xx with JSON error body when file is missing from uploads dir
src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not increment download count when file is missing (5xx)
criteria_coverage.notes: Status >= 500, JSON content-type, error body asserted; counter re-read to verify no increment.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC5: Successful 200 delivery increments counter by exactly 1 and persists
tests: src/lib/store/__tests__/resource-store.test.ts :: incrementDownload increments downloadCount by exactly 1
src/lib/store/__tests__/resource-store.test.ts :: subsequent calls each increment by 1
src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: increments counter by 2 under two concurrent successful requests
criteria_coverage.notes: Store-level and route-level increments are verified. Persistence is exercised indirectly: writes go to JSON on disk and a subsequent getResourceById round-trips through the file. There is no explicit single-request-through-route → count==1 assertion (only the concurrent case), but the store test + concurrent route test collectively cover the requirement.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC6: Failed downloads (4xx, 5xx, aborted) do not increment counter
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not increment download count on 401
src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not increment download count when file is missing (5xx)
criteria_coverage.notes: 401 and 5xx paths are covered. 404-path no-increment is NOT explicitly asserted (a bug that always incremented after getResourceById returned null would slip past). Client-abort mid-stream also not tested, but that is called out as an edge case not a hard AC. Non-blocking: recommend adding a 404 no-increment assertion.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC7: Two concurrent successful downloads → counter increases by exactly 2 (no lost updates)
tests: src/lib/store/__tests__/resource-store.test.ts :: two concurrent increments both apply — final count === 2
src/app/api/resources/[id]/download/__tests__/route.test.ts :: increments counter by 2 under two concurrent successful requests
criteria_coverage.notes: Store and route both exercise Promise.all concurrency and assert final count == 2.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC8: Each successful download creates an audit record with resourceId, userId, timestamp
tests: src/lib/store/__tests__/resource-store.test.ts :: writes an audit record with matching resourceId, userId, and timestamp
criteria_coverage.notes: Reads audit.json, asserts length 1 and all three required fields present with correct values. Timestamp is only asserted as non-empty string (not ISO 8601 parseable), but contract only requires 'non-empty'. Fine.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC9: Resource detail view displays the current total download count
criteria_coverage.notes: BLOCKING: No test targets the resource detail view (src/app/resources/[id]/page.tsx or equivalent). Only the metadata API (GET /api/resources/[id]) is tested — it returns the count, but there is no test that the detail UI actually renders it. A page that fetched the resource and then failed to render downloadCount would pass the current suite.

src/components/__tests__/ResourceCard.test.tsx :: renders both name and count without error

tests: src/app/api/resources/metrics/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 200 with only the authenticated owner's resources
src/app/api/resources/metrics/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 401 with JSON error body for unauthenticated request
src/lib/store/__tests__/resource-store.test.ts :: getResourcesByOwner returns only resources matching the given ownerId

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC12: Admin flow can retrieve download metrics across resources
criteria_coverage.notes: No test for an admin cross-owner metrics view. Note: contract.md explicitly defers admin cross-owner view ('Not in contract: admin cross-owner view (deferred)'). Interpreting this as a scope carve-out by the contract-writer, not a testing failure — flagging as non-blocking but leaving it as an unmapped criterion for visibility.

criteria_coverage.criterion: AC13: Download URL and responses do not expose internal storage paths
tests: src/app/api/resources/[id]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not expose filePath in the response body
src/app/api/resources/metrics/__tests__/route.test.ts :: does not include filePath in any returned resource
criteria_coverage.notes: Both surfaces (metadata + metrics) assert filePath is undefined AND that the literal secret path substring is absent from the serialised JSON. Download URL itself (/api/resources/[id]/download) uses the resource id, not a path — structurally satisfies the AC.

test_findings.test: returns 200 with PDF content-type and content-disposition when resource and file exist
test_findings.issue: Content-Disposition assertions only check that the header contains 'attachment' and the resource name substring. They do not assert the filename has a .pdf extension (contract: filename="<sanitisedName>.pdf"), that the filename is quoted, or that sanitisation actually ran end-to-end (e.g., a resource named 'bad";filename=evil' should not produce two filename params). Recommend adding one route-level test with a resource name containing a quote/semicolon to prove sanitisation is wired into the route, not just the utility.

AC6 says failed 4xx downloads must not increment. 401 no-increment is covered but 404 no-increment is not. A bug that ordered incrementDownload before the not-found check would pass the current suite (it would throw on unknown id, which happens to protect us, but the intent is not asserted).

Contract specifies three branches: TEST_USER_ID → cookie → null. Only branches 1 and 3 are tested. If a coder omitted the cookie branch entirely, tests would still pass. Since the download route depends on getSessionUser and there is a fallback env-based path used in tests, this is not blocking, but it is a spec-fidelity gap.

Does not explicitly assert that no PDF bytes are delivered on 401 (only that status is 401 and content-type is JSON). Adequate but strengthenable by asserting body.error is present AND response body is not application/pdf.

Timestamp only asserted as non-empty string. Ticket edge cases and contract intent imply ISO 8601. Consider asserting Number.isFinite(Date.parse(audit[0].timestamp)) to catch a bug where a Date object is stringified as '[object Object]' or an epoch number is written.

unmapped_tests.notes: Maps to AC1 (filename in Content-Disposition) via the sanitisation edge cases in ticket 'Filename safety'. Not a criterion of its own but supporting coverage — legitimate.

unmapped_tests.test: src/app/api/resources/[id]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 200 with resource data and download count
unmapped_tests.notes: Not tied to a specific AC — supports the detail view (AC9) as a data source but does not itself prove AC9. Legitimate as a contract-level test.

unmapped_criteria.criterion: AC9: Resource detail view displays the current total download count
unmapped_criteria.reason: No test exists for the detail-view UI. Only the API that would feed it is tested. BLOCKING for this round.

unmapped_criteria.criterion: AC12: Admin flow can retrieve download metrics across resources
unmapped_criteria.reason: Contract.md explicitly defers 'admin cross-owner view'. If this deferral is intentional (i.e., ticket AC12 is being pushed to a follow-up), the plan/contract should say so explicitly and the AC checkbox should be reflected accordingly. Non-blocking here because it is a documented contract-level scope decision, but flagged so it is not silently dropped.

one_line_summary: Solid coverage for auth, 401/404/5xx paths, counter atomicity, audit, filePath leak prevention, and ResourceCard; blocking gap on AC9 (no test for resource detail view rendering the download count), plus a documented scope carve-out on AC12 (admin metrics) that should be surfaced explicitly.
